TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Rear support area
DATE 16 November 2028 · 0630 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 85 min, closes at 128
Supply class Australian replenishment ship. Photo: Nick-D · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"During deployment, it is too late to practice battlefield sustainment skills."
- Gen. Gustave F. Perna, US Army Materiel Command, 2019

REAR SUPPORT AREA, Coral Sea, east of Cape York. COLLINS has been out for thirty-five days and comes home next week whatever happens today. She is surfaced alongside STALWART taking fuel, stores and torpedoes, and putting two crew across for medical, and while she is up there she is a very large grey target making four knots.

The service window is thirty-five minutes and it runs on the clock, not on how much crossed the hose. What crosses is real: STALWART passes COLLINS her torpedoes, and any escort that comes inside half a mile at twelve knots or less can take missiles back across - she will pass anything up to an NSM, a Tomahawk or an SM-6 - for as long as her magazines last. STALWART and COLLINS have to be inside the service box - five miles around the rendezvous - when the window closes; what you do with them in between is your judgement, and the clock does not stop for you. Hold it and your ships are rearmed before the Banda convoy on the twentieth; miss it and they sail that convoy on what they have left. When the thirty-five minutes are up, both of them go together to the withdrawal line eighteen miles south, and COLLINS dives the moment she is clear of the hose.
STALWART has the duty. MV Coral Provider was pencilled in with the dry stores; she sails only if SUPPLY survived the Gulf of Papua passage in October.

A Russian Tu-214R came down the outside of the box last night and did not go home, which usually means somebody now knows where to look. She is off the scope for now: expect her back over the box about five minutes in, with the Akula that is unaccounted for to the south-east closing behind her. There is also a Flanker pair within range of here with a Helix spotting for them off a tender that has been loitering north of the box since Tuesday. Assume one of those Flankers is carrying something for a ship. Keep the window open and get everybody out of it.

SERVICE DETAIL: Collins uses the collection's actual Collins hull and begins on the surface at the rendezvous. Collins and Stalwart both have the four-knot service telegraph selected. They creep south inside the box during the check; after the 35-minute signal, order withdrawal speed and depth yourself. The clock does not verify depth.

KILA: A light Russian corvette is approaching from the north-east, expected about twelve minutes into the window. Her missiles make her a real surface threat. The trawler remains a separate identification problem. Keep a surface screen while the flight and Poseidon work VICTOR.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Commodore Alex Mercer; Commander Mara Kila for the eastern route
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Protect Stalwart and Collins at the service rendezvous. Both must be inside the area for the 35-minute check and then withdraw south together. Collins is exposed while surfaced, and enemy reconnaissance has been reported nearby. Keep the approaches covered and bring both vessels out.
• Have STALWART and COLLINS inside the service area at 35 minutes, then bring both to the southern withdrawal line
• HMAS Collins must survive
• HMAS Stalwart must survive

HMAS Stalwart, HMAS Collins surfaced for service, your escort and her flight; one P-8 from Scherger if tasked. Opposing, all Russian: one Akula, one Tu-214R, a Flanker pair with a Ka-27RLD spotting for them, and an armed intelligence trawler keeping station on the group. A light Russian Steregushchiy-class corvette approaches after twelve minutes.

The planned window is 85 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 43 minutes more; the operation is closed at 128 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
